_comment: Example config snippets to copy into config.json. Each entry's value is a drop-in replacement for the matching top-level key (e.g. the "esp32" block). After editing config.json, restart the daemon — it re-renders these, captures the frames and re-uploads the recordings to the ESP32 (no reflash; the device skips the write if nothing changed).

button_spread_power_on_off._comment: Experimental power-button light-spread effects. button_on bursts a white front out of the button end of the strip and spreads it in, then settles into a breathing pulse; button_off flies the lit strip back into the button. 'origin' says where the button sits along the strip, 0..1 (0 = index-0 end, 1 = last-index end, 0.5 = center — the light radiates out of / collapses into the middle from both sides at once); when 'origin' is absent, 'reverse' picks an end (default true). 'palette' lays comma-separated colour stops out by distance from the button (first stop at the button, last at the farthest pixel), so e.g. a rainbow expands as bands radiating out of the button and gets gathered back in on shutdown; keep the two palettes identical so off mirrors on. A single colour ('color', legacy) is a one-stop palette. The button_on intro is recorded for spread_seconds + period_seconds/2 so it ends at the pulse's dim trough, and breathe opens at that same trough (matching period_seconds + min_brightness), so the handoff and the breathe loop are seamless. If the spread comes from the wrong place on the real strip, adjust origin on both effects (keep the two in sync so on and off share the same source point).

lava_lamp_idle._comment: A 'lava lamp' idle: soft metaball blobs drift along the strip, and where two overlap their fields add into a brighter, hotter spot. The blobs are intensity-driven — faint edges sample the start of a palette window, hot overlapping cores its end — and that window slides along the palette over time (color_speed), so the whole scene cycles smoothly through every color. This entry is one object for the "rules" array — drop it in as the last (catch-all, no "if") rule, replacing the default cycle, or insert it earlier behind your own condition. Warm sweep shown here; for a cool 'blue goo' lamp set palette "1038c8,1ea0ff,90f0ff". The blobs start uniformly spaced and visibly separate, then drift and merge; keep radius below about 0.5/blobs to preserve that separation. Fewer/larger blobs (blobs 3, radius 0.15) read as a slow lamp; more/smaller (blobs 6, radius 0.07) as a busier bubbling. color_span is how much palette a blob spans (1.0 = whole palette, no sliding); 'core' is the field that maps to the window's hot end / full brightness — lower it for fatter, hotter blobs. white_hot blooms a strong overlap toward white-hot (a rare hard pileup flashes pure white, ordinary merges only white-tip); set it to 0 to keep overlaps fully palette-colored.

lava_preset_pack._comment: Three ready-made lava moods, as entries for a cycle's "effects" array (or lift one's settings into a rule of its own). deep_sea: near-black water with cyan/teal/green bioluminescent blobs, blooms kept subtle. nebula: many big violet/magenta/blue clouds that overlap constantly, so the strip is a slowly churning nebula rather than separate blobs. candlelight: two lazy amber blobs over a warm dark base — the calmest of the three, close to candle glow without any flicker.
